artworks.title: The Meeting of Orestes and Hermione
artworks.description: Girodet's Cleveland drawing isolates the Spartan princess with her cousin Orestes — the marriage Tyndareus promised and Menelaus later complicated with Neoptolemus. Neoclassical line makes Hermione a figure of contested succession: Helen's daughter as the prize that binds Atreid and Aeacid claims after Troy. The sheet is among the rare images that name her without Racine's Andromache crowding the frame.

artworks.title: Andromaque et Pyrrhus
artworks.description: Guérin's Louvre canvas (INV 5183) stages Racine's Andromaque: Pyrrhus between Andromache and the jealous Hermione, Helen's daughter who will drive Orestes to murder. Painted for the Salon that made Guérin's name, it fixes Hermione as the tragic third of the Epirote triangle — the princess whose wounded pride ends a dynasty. The painting remains the defining modern image of her theatrical afterlife.

music.title: Ermione
music.description: Rossini's azione tragica for Naples, after Racine, gives Hermione the title role — the Spartan princess who orders Pyrrhus' death and collapses when Orestes obeys. Withdrawn after seven nights, it later became the composer's 'little Italian Guillaume Tell.'

popCulture.title: Andromaque
popCulture.creator: Jean Racine
popCulture.description: Racine's tragedy makes Hermione the jealous axis of Pyrrhus, Andromache, and Orestes — the French stage's lasting portrait of Helen's daughter as passion and revenge.

popCulture.title: Andromache
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' play sets Hermione against Andromache in Phthia — the childless Spartan wife who asks Menelaus to kill Hector's widow, the oldest theatrical dossier of her cruelty and fear.
